intro: Probation officers read people, solve complex cases and make firm decisions, all valued in public service and compliance. The closest of the 25 careers below is First-Line Supervisors of Correctional Officers, with an 83% skill match and a BLS May 2025 median of $77,970, which is 18% more than the $66,270 probation officers earn.
why_it_works: A caseload means judging risk, writing reports for court and helping people change direction. O*NET rates social perceptiveness at 4 out of 5 for this job and complex problem solving at 3.75. Social service management, compliance and special education draw on the same skills. Almost every match needs no extra schooling. The common gaps are coordinating programs, teaching and managing people and resources.
tips: Present your caseload work as case management and compliance; both terms are used in the jobs that match you.
Compliance Officers earn $80,730, or 22% more, and use your eye for rules and reports.
Ask your agency about supervisor tracks; correctional supervisors are your closest match.

faq.q: What jobs can former probation officers do?
faq.a: The closest matches are correctional officer supervisors (83%), Social and Community Service Managers (81%) and equal opportunity officers (78%), based on O*NET 31.0. Social and Community Service Managers earn $80,390, which is 21% more than the probation officer median.

faq.q: Which careers for probation officers pay more?
faq.a: 14 of the 25 matches pay more than $66,270. Police and detective supervisors earn $106,040 (60% more), Registered Nurses $97,550 (47% more) and Labor Relations Specialists $95,420 (44% more), according to BLS May 2025 data. Nursing requires a nursing degree and license.

faq.q: Do probation officers need another degree?
faq.a: Usually not. 24 of the 25 matches need no more education than probation officers already have, and only 1 usually needs a graduate degree. A bachelor's degree is common, held by 50% of workers in a close match, so your current degree usually qualifies you.

faq.q: What skills should probation officers learn?
faq.a: The skills that most often need work are coordination, instructing, managing materials and managing people. Judgment already rates 3.62 out of 5 for probation officers in O*NET, so supervising staff and running programs are the next steps for the better-paid roles on this page.
